title: Iwaki — いわき
goal: Recognise country/language words and distinguish speaking, saying and listening.

cards.title: The Modern City Name Uses Hiragana

blocks.text: The current city name is **いわき市 / いわきし**, with いわき written in hiragana. Iwaki is a coastal city associated with places such as Aquamarine Fukushima and Iwaki Yumoto hot springs. Our practice dialogue occurs in an invented learning encounter.
**いわきで友だちに会いました。** いわきで ともだちに あいました。 — I met a friend in Iwaki.

We do not invent kanji for a hiragana city label to satisfy a template. Instead, the next card explains a related historical spelling that learners may encounter, clearly distinguished from the official modern city name.

items: **Character:** 磐 · **Meaning/reading:** large rock; いわ, ハン/バン · **Radical/components:** 石, いし, below 般, a historical sound component; 般 visibly contains 舟-like and 殳-like sections · **Role:** Assisted historical-name encounter.
**Character:** 城 · **Meaning/reading:** castle; しろ, ジョウ; き in 磐城 · **Radical/components:** 土, つちへん + 成, historical sound element · **Role:** Encounter review from 宮城/castle words.

blocks.text: **磐城 / いわき** is a related historical regional spelling, not a replacement instruction for modern **いわき市**. Contrast **岩手 / いわて**: 岩 and 磐 share rock-related meanings and 石 connections but are different characters. We test recognition of the modern label and sensible component understanding, not writing the rare historical name from memory.

**国 / くに — country; 外国 / がいこく — foreign country; 外国人 / がいこくじん — foreign person/foreigner.** 国 has radical **囗**, くにがまえ, enclosing a modern **玉**. The enclosing radical is larger than ordinary 口; its position around another component matters.
**日本は国です。** にほんは くにです。 — Japan is a country.

**外国の本 / がいこくのほん — a book from/about a foreign country**, depending on context. 外 and 人 are review. 人 is じん in 外国人/日本人, but ひと as a standalone person and にん in 三人. Learn the useful whole compounds rather than assign 人 one permanent sound.

cards.title: 語: A Language in Common Words

blocks.text: **日本語 / にほんご — Japanese language; 英語 / えいご — English language.** 英 stays assisted here. 語 has radical **言**, ごんべん, on the left and **吾**, a historical sound component, on the right. 吾 visibly includes 五 and 口; five mouths is not a definition of language.
**これは日本語の本です。** これは にほんごの ほんです。 — This is a book in/about Japanese, in our stated language-learning context.
日本 is the country name; 日本語 is the language name; 日本人 is a Japanese person. The final component changes the word's category. Do not substitute these three whole words merely because they share 日本.

**話す / はなす — speak/talk; 話します / はなします — speak/will speak.** 話 has radical **言**, ごんべん, and **舌**, a historical sound component with a useful speech-related association. 舌's visible upper strokes and lower 口 are nested recognition pieces, not a reading formula for はなす.
**日本語を話します。** にほんごを はなします。 — I speak Japanese.
**友だちと話します。** ともだちと はなします。 — I talk with a friend.

The language uses を as the spoken-language object in our model; the conversation partner uses と. This と is a partner/companion relationship, extending earlier companion patterns. It is not the と used to quote what someone says.
**言う / いう — say; 言います / いいます — say/will say.** 言 is its own radical, いう/ことば; when on the left its form is called ごんべん. It has stacked upper strokes and lower 口.
**「こんにちは」と言います。** 「こんにちは」と いいます。 — I say “hello.”

Here **と** marks the quoted words. The exact quotation is 「こんにちは」. Compare **友だちと話します**, where と names the conversation partner, and **りんごと水**, where it joins nouns. The same particle can express different relationships; the surrounding words clarify it.
The limited quotation pattern is newly taught here. Broader reported statements, 思う and plain-form quotation are reserved for later.

**電話 / でんわ — telephone; phone call.** 電 was formally studied in Sendai; 話 is formal now. The compound reads でんわ, while 話す reads はなす. A kanji can connect a device word and an action without keeping the same reading.
**電話で友だちと話します。** でんわで ともだちと はなします。 — I talk with a friend on the phone.

で marks the means/channel, like 電車で for transport and 目で for seeing. The lesson does not require **電話する** as an unexplained new する verb. Use the already taught 話す action in a natural sentence and learn 電話 as a useful noun.

items: **Action:** speak · **Nonpast:** 話します · **Negative:** 話しません · **Past:** 話しました · **Past negative:** 話しませんでした
**Action:** say · **Nonpast:** 言います · **Negative:** 言いません · **Past:** 言いました · **Past negative:** 言いませんでした

blocks.text: Readings: はなします/はなしません/はなしました/はなしませんでした; いいます/いいません/いいました/いいませんでした.
**友だちと日本語で話しました。** ともだちと にほんごで はなしました。 — I talked with a friend in Japanese.

Language **で** can mark the language used as a medium. Compare **日本語を話しました**, I spoke Japanese. Both are natural, so tests must supply a sentence relationship that clearly distinguishes language object from medium.
**全然 / ぜんぜん — not at all**, paired with a negative predicate in the beginner pattern. 全/然 remain assisted characters; the word is part of the supplied frequency/degree syllabus.
**英語は全然話しません。** えいごは ぜんぜん はなしません。 — I do not speak English at all, describing this fictional person's usage/habit.

This is **not a statement of inability**. “I cannot speak English” requires a capability pattern we have not yet formally taught. Do not translate 話しません as “cannot.” Contrast **時々、日本語を話します**, I sometimes speak Japanese. The adverbs give different frequency/degree information; the verb ending gives negation.

**おはようございます — good morning; こんにちは — hello/good afternoon; こんばんは — good evening; ごめんなさい — sorry.** These complete the greeting set specified in the supplied syllabus, alongside the already used すみません/ありがとうございます and meal/shop phrases. **こんにちは/こんばんは** end in written **は**, pronounced **わ** in these expressions.
**友だちに「こんにちは」と言いました。** ともだちに「こんにちは」と いいました。 — I said “hello” to a friend.

に identifies the person addressed; と marks the quoted words. In an evening version use こんばんは. We do not equate every “sorry” situation with one phrase; these are the basic expressions for the stated scenes.

items: What is the current city label: いわき市 or a required replacement 磐城市? **Answer:** いわき市.
Read 国, 日本語, 英語 and 電話. **Answer:** くに; にほんご; えいご; でんわ.
Which component links 語 and 話? **Answer:** 言.
Complete the quotation: 「こんにちは」＿言います。 **Answer:** と.
In 英語は全然話しません, does 話しません mean inability? **Answer:** No; it states not speaking, in the supplied usage context.
Make 話します past negative. **Answer:** 話しませんでした / はなしませんでした.

blocks.text: いわき市 uses hiragana. 磐城 is an assisted historical connection, not a replacement city spelling. 国 is くに; 日本語 is the language; 日本人 is a person. 語/話 share 言; 話す is はなす, 言う is いう. と can mark a partner, noun list or exact quotation. 全然 pairs with a negative here; habitual negation is different from inability.

**Recall task:** “I said hello to a friend and talked in Japanese.” **Model:** 友だちに「こんにちは」と言いました。日本語で話しました。 Fukushima's four lessons are complete. Read and test. Package 05 next begins Ibaraki / 茨城 / いばらき.
